headline: Digital passport progress, CSRD assurance consultation, and proposed downstream CBAM expansion
summary: The EU published technical resources and a joint EU-China white paper on Digital Product Passport interoperability. Meanwhile, the Commission opened a consultation on CSRD limited assurance standards and outlined plans to extend CBAM to downstream metal products.

items.title: Technical resources and EU-China white paper published for Digital Product Passports
items.what: The European Commission published six technical resources for connecting to the Digital Product Passport registry, alongside a joint EU-China white paper on DPP data interoperability.
items.meaning: Clarifies data connectivity standards between EU importers and Chinese manufacturers, which is vital for preparing your battery platform and power tool portfolio for DPP requirements.
items.action: Share technical specifications with IT and Chinese supplier management teams to align data exchange protocols.

sources.title: Commission publishes six technical resources for companies connecting to the digital product passport registry
China, EU release DPP interoperability white paper to facilitate data connectivity

items.title: Commission consults on CSRD limited assurance standards
items.what: The European Commission launched a consultation on standards for limited assurance of sustainability reporting under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive.
items.meaning: Directly impacts your CSRD compliance strategy by defining the criteria external auditors will apply when verifying your sustainability metrics and Chinese supplier data.
items.action: Review consultation topics with internal audit leads to ensure sustainability data collection meets audit standards.

sources.title: EU CSRD: Commission consults on limited assurance standards, Julia Voskoboinikova

items.title: Commission proposes CBAM expansion to downstream steel and aluminium products
items.what: The European Commission proposed extending CBAM to 180 downstream products and finalized rules for deducting third-country carbon costs, recognizing China's emissions trading scheme.
items.meaning: Although finished packaged goods are currently exempt, extending CBAM to downstream steel and aluminium items could directly impact imported power tools or components from China.
items.action: Review the proposed list of 180 downstream products against your import tariff codes.

sources.title: EU industrial emissions fall as Commission outlines proposed CBAM extension to 180 downstream steel and aluminium products

items.title: Corrigendum published for EU Machinery Regulation
items.what: The EU published an official corrigendum to Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery, introducing technical corrections.
items.meaning: As the brand manufacturer of powered tools and equipment, your technical documentation must reflect the updated text ahead of the January 2027 application date.
items.action: Inform product compliance teams to check technical file references against the corrected text.
